Project brief & requirements

PROBLEM · OBJECTIVES · COVERAGE

Problem statement

Purchase behaviour in online retail is driven by several measurable factors (engagement, cart activity, prior spend, membership). This project identifies the strongest drivers of Purchase_Amount and builds models that predict spend and classify high spenders, so that behavioural patterns can be quantified rather than guessed.

Objectives

  • Load, clean and profile a 20,000-record customer dataset.
  • Identify significant relationships between customer variables and spend.
  • Apply descriptive statistics, probability, Bayes' theorem and hypothesis testing.
  • Compute Pearson and Spearman correlations with a correlation matrix.
  • Develop simple and multiple linear regression models and compare them.
  • Implement matrix operations and gradient descent, then optimise with trees and forests.
  • Evaluate every model with MAE, MSE, RMSE, R² and residual analysis.
The source document's student-performance example is a task template; this dashboard applies the same eight tasks to project idea #8 — E-Commerce Customer Purchase Behaviour Analysis.

TASK 1 · CLEANING

What was fixed

06 Linear algebra with NumPy

TASK 6 · MATRICES

Vector & matrix operations

NumPy EQUIVALENT
Vector addition: a + b = [a₁+b₁, a₂+b₂, …]
Dot product: a · b = Σᵢ aᵢbᵢ
Matrix multiplication: (XᵀX)ⱼₖ = Σᵢ Xᵢⱼ · Xᵢₖ
Design matrix: X = [1, Time, Visits, Pages, Cart, Prev] → 16,000 × 6
Regression calculation: θ = (XᵀX)⁻¹ Xᵀy and ŷ = X·θ

07 Calculus & gradient descent

TASK 7 · OPTIMIZATION

Cost function & derivative

CALCULUS
Cost: J(θ) = (1 / 2m) · Σᵢ (Xθ − y)ᵢ²
Derivative: ∂J/∂θⱼ = (1 / m) · Σᵢ (Xθ − y)ᵢ · Xᵢⱼ
Update rule: θⱼ ← θⱼ − α · ∂J/∂θⱼ
Convergence: repeat until the cost stops decreasing, then compare θ with the normal-equation solution.

Parameter trajectory

α = 0.05 · 200 ITERS
Iterβ₀β₁ Timeβ₂ CartCost

      Action
      —
      Data20,600 raw rows → 20,000 clean rows (13 columns, seed 42). 600 duplicates dropped; 2,063 missing values filled with training-only medians/modes (16,000 train / 4,000 test).
      What is not in the dataAll records are synthetically generated in Python (ecommerce_project.py); not real customer transactions. Discount_Percent, Review_Rating and Age are simulated independently.
      Model limitsMultiple OLS (5 features) and batch gradient descent (α=0.05, 1000 iters) assume linear additive effects; Shapiro-Wilk p=0.0188 on n=4,000 test residuals shows slight tail departure. CART trees and forests in the ML Lab are trained locally in the browser on the same split with a fixed seed.
